en.html:
Ji, that is so.

Beginning toh from that man's return only. So long away from the village, and back he comes with shogunate magistrate attached to his name.

Our little village, a specially sent magistrate? Arre, why this much government affection suddenly? Strange business. Trouble also, I thought. Still, born here only. Apna hi aadmi. One of ours. With this small blanket we covered our worry.

Then Nagasaka arrived with his men, gathered all the village officials and announced: mountain khodenge. We will dig up the mountain.

Haan. The mountain. A valuable vein sleeps inside it, an old story says. In the Tokugawa days, a hunter found a precious stone up there.

Villagers delighted. Prospectors called. Spades almost running to the place by themselves. But the Emishi clan living on the mountain stopped them.

According to the Emishi, that stone was Konjin's anger made into substance. Take it out and you call the curse down on your own head. Seedha warning. Very clear.

But money had begun speaking; who would hear a mere human voice? Nothing here then, nothing here now. A money-growing tree suddenly appeared and our people could think only of shaking it. So they followed the prospectors and began the tunnel.

...Aur shaap aa gaya. The curse came.

Near the vein, almost there, and lightning burst out of the mountain. Raced everywhere like a storm. Whoever the light touched...

Stone, some say. Sand, others say. Rusted away, that version also. Different accounts. Many people died, however. Ismein doubt nahin. Records from those days leave no doubt.

Now the villagers remembered the Emishi possessed ears one could speak into. Called the chief. Please, save us, calm this curse. Advice we would not take, rescue we required immediately. Convenient, haan. But they accepted without a word, so we have heard.

Their ancestral sacred treasure they put in the tunnel. Like a weight to hold Konjin's force down. Then filled it in again. Perhaps that settled it. Ek baar aaya, phir nahin. The curse came that once, no more.

Even afterward our people could not feel safe. A shrine they built on the mountain, gave it to the Emishi and asked them to worship the cursing god. Still going on. Old and worn now, the shrine. The Emishi also, far fewer remain...

Yeh hua history. Such is the history.

And THIS taboo Nagasaka wished to put his hands into. A new hole meant time and money. Why pay for fresh trouble when old trouble is already available? Records he studied. Dig out the old tunnel: that was his plan.

Naturally, all of us objected. Not every villager believes the curse. Such an old story, kitna sach, kitna added afterward? I myself have doubts.

But suppose all goes well. Vein found. What comes to us? Miners' lives. Hard labour. Our share only that. A little profit returning from Rokuhara to the village? Us Rokuhara se? Madam, allow me some disbelief.

If the curse is entirely true, then of course another kind of misery. Whichever way, our heads only under the falling thing.

For objecting, sword mila. What drove him so far, I do not know. Several who opposed him were killed. The previous headman also... Ji. My elder brother. Before this, I only kept a general store.

Once force begins, what contest can we offer? Few shogunate soldiers, yes, but suspicious fellows came with them. Bodyguards, perhaps. Terribly strong, those men. Small numbers became very large when one had to stand against them.

So we obeyed. Digging began. Hard work, hardly any rest. Overwork took people. Punishments took people. 'Instruction,' they called it. Such education, and afterward a household had one person less. How many died...

Resist, die. Obey, die. Gaon jaaye toh jaaye kahan? Where was the village to go? Work, though, proceeded beautifully. As though Bhagwan had collected every blessing due to us and sent the whole parcel to Nagasaka. I cannot have been the only one crying into his pillow from helpless anger.

While we were suffering like that...
Madam Inspector, you came.

ja.html:
――左様でございます。
　そもそもの始まりは、長らく村を離れていたあの男
が、幕府代官の肩書きを引っさげて帰ってきたときの
こと。

　こんな小村にわざわざ代官が派遣されてくるなんて
おかしな話でございますし、厄介にも思いましたが、
それでも村の出身者というのが救いかと、最初はその
程度に考えておりました。

　しかしすぐ度肝を抜かれる羽目になったのでござい
ます。
　あの男、長坂は手勢を連れて乗り込んで来るや否や
村の諸役を集め、お山を掘ると言い放ったのですから。

　はい。
　あの山には貴重な鉱脈が眠っているという言い伝え
がございまして――昔、まだ徳川さまが天下を治めて
おられた頃、猟師が山で貴石を発見したということが。

　当時の村の人々は喜んで、山師を呼び寄せ、早速に
掘り出そうとしたようでございます。
　しかし、山に住んでいた<ruby>蝦夷<rt>えみし</rt></ruby>の一族がその前に立ち
塞がり、制止しました。

　なんでも猟師が発見した石は、蝦夷の言うところに
よると、<ruby>こんじんさま<rt>・・・・・・</rt></ruby>の怒りの気なのだとか。
　それを掘り返すなど、望んで祟りを招くに等しいと。

　そう言われてもピンと来なかったのでしょう、村人
達は耳を貸さず、山師に従って坑道を掘り始めました。
　今も昔も何もない村のこと、やにわに金のなる木を
見つけて躍起になっていたのかもしれません。

　……そうして、祟りが降り注いだのでございます。

　それはそれは恐ろしい有様だったそうで。
　もうすぐ鉱脈に行き当たろうかというある時、不意
に山から稲光が迸るや、嵐のように辺りを駆け巡り、
その光に触れた者は皆……

　石になったやら、砂になったやら、<ruby>錆びてしまった<rt>・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>
やら、色々と伝えられておりますが。
　確かなことは、多くの者が亡くなったという、これ
は当時の記録からも疑いようのない事実でございます。

　村の者どもは慌てふためき、蝦夷の長を招いて祟り
を鎮めてくれるよう懇願しました。
　虫の良い言い草というものですが、蝦夷は何も口に
せず頼みを聞いてくれたと伝え聞いております。

　一族伝来の神宝を坑道の中に安置して<ruby>こんじんさま<rt>・・・・・・</rt></ruby>
の気を止める重石とし、その上で坑道を埋め戻したの
だそうで。
　その甲斐あってか、祟りは一度きりで絶えました。

　それでも村人は安心できなかったのでしょう、更に
山へ社を建てて蝦夷に預け、祟り神を祀らせました。
　これは今もまだ続いております。社は古ぼけ、蝦夷
はだいぶん数を減らしてしまいましたが……。

　そんなことがあったのでございます。

　この禁忌に、長坂は手をつけると云うのですよ。
　一から穴を掘るのでは金も時間も掛かりますからな。
記録を調べて、昔の坑道を掘り返そうという計画で。

　もちろん、誰もが反対しました。
　それは何も皆が皆、祟りを信じ込んでいた為という
のではございません。何しろ昔の話ですし、何がどこ
まで真実かは怪しいと、私なども思っております。

　しかしでございます。仮に首尾良く鉱脈を発見した
としても、待っているのは、鉱夫としての過酷な生活
だけでございましょう？　<ruby>あの<rt>・・</rt></ruby>六波羅がまさか、
収益の一部でも村へ還元してくれるとは思えませんし。

　そしてもし、祟りの伝説が全て事実だったなら……。
　おわかりでございましょう。長坂の計画はどう転ん
でも、村を不幸にしかしないのでございます。

　皆の不賛同は、刃で報われました。
　何が彼をそこまで駆り立てたのかはわかりませんが、
異を唱えた者が何人も殺され、先代の村長も……ええ、
私はその弟です。それまではただの雑貨屋でしたよ。

　力ずくで来られては、勝負になりますものか。代官
が連れてきた幕府の兵はさほど多くなかったのですが、
ほかにも怪しげな連中が幾人かおりまして。用心棒と
でもいうのでしょうかな。それがまた、滅法強く……。

　止むを得ず私どもは長坂に従い、お山を掘り始めた
のでございます。ろくに休みもなしの、苛酷な作業で
ございました。過労や、指導と称する奴らの制裁で、
また何人が死んだことか……。

　刃向かえば死。従っても死。
　村は追い込まれておりましたが、忌々しくも作業の
方は順調でした。長坂一人を神様が嘉したかのようで、
悔しさに枕を濡らしたのは私だけではありますまい。

　そうして難儀していたところに……
　巡察官さま、貴方がやって来られたのでございます。

en.html:
Fair size, the headman's house. Reception room large enough for a sumo bout. Rich man demonstrating his power? Zaroori nahin. Not necessarily. More likely the village simply had land to spare.

No conspicuous dirt. Reception room, after all. Tasteful furnishings also, none. Everything plain. Generations of headmen had lived here and this much their house amounted to. Poverty had already made its statement; asking for further details seemed unnecessary.

The headman looked uneasy. Bare room, perhaps he was ashamed. Personally the lack of ornament suited me. Say so, though, and what would he hear? 'Aapki gareebi bahut pasand aayi.' I liked his poverty very much.

A most helpful guest. The man had not selected poverty as an interior design preference.

Besides, the cause probably lay elsewhere. Unknown outsider myself, my presence was not entirely innocent. His eyes, however, had been on the other visitor for some time.

ja.html:
村長の家はまずまずの大きさで、通された応接間も
相撲くらいはできそうな広さがあった。といっても、
それは主人の財権力ゆえというより単に土地が余って
いるからというのが理由ではないだろうか。

　応接間だけに見苦しい汚れが目立つなどということ
はないが、気の利いた調度があるわけでもなかった。
　ごく質素な装いである。代々の村長が住まいとした
家にしてこれということからも、村の貧しさは窺えた。

　部屋の味気なさを恥じてか、村長は気後れしている
ようにも見えた。俺の嗜好で言えばこの飾り気の無さ
はむしろ好ましい。がそう口にしても、趣味でやって
いるわけではない村長にすれば喜べないだろう。

　それに実際のところ、村長が本当に気後れしている
のだとするなら、理由はもっと他にありそうだった。
　得体の知れない外来人（俺）も潔白ではなかろうが。
村長の視線は先刻から、もう一人の来客の上にあった。

en.html: A young woman. Beautiful, haan. Giving her that much credit required no struggle. Gloss in the long hair, teacup lifted just so, smile without effort. Good upbringing had taken care of the small movements also. Behind her, an elderly woman sat in attendance with exemplary obviousness. Sheltered, highborn lady. A perfect picture. Except one item in the picture was refusing to behave. Item? Defect, I had almost said. Galat. It spoiled nothing. The uniform suited her. It suited her so well that the matter became more puzzling. Modern uniform, not Warring States armour. Still, hardness, unease, ill omen—the old smell remained. On this woman, though, no clash. The cup was delicate, the smile was gentle, the whole military arrangement fitted beside both without an argument. Uniform mein kuch khaas bhi nahin tha. Nothing unusual about it.◆ ...A foolish question from my side.
en.text:
A young woman. Beautiful, haan. Giving her that much credit required no struggle. Gloss in the long hair, teacup lifted just so, smile without effort. Good upbringing had taken care of the small movements also. Behind her, an elderly woman sat in attendance with exemplary obviousness.

Sheltered, highborn lady. A perfect picture. Except one item in the picture was refusing to behave.

Item? Defect, I had almost said. Galat. It spoiled nothing. The uniform suited her. It suited her so well that the matter became more puzzling.

Modern uniform, not Warring States armour. Still, hardness, unease, ill omen—the old smell remained. On this woman, though, no clash. The cup was delicate, the smile was gentle, the whole military arrangement fitted beside both without an argument.

Uniform mein kuch khaas bhi nahin tha. Nothing unusual about it.◆

...A foolish question from my side.

en.html:
She suited the uniform. That was all. Unease and ill omen she had brought from home. Whatever she looked like, a soldier she unquestionably was.

The headman had been there for the gunshot. If he remembered that, surely he was not mistaking her for a lady in fancy dress. Then the source of his discomfort must be the affiliation shown by her uniform.

The International Union for Harmonious Coexistence and Prosperity. Yamato Occupation Forces General Headquarters. GHQ.

Until six years ago, the enemy our whole nation had fought. Now a body of foreigners installed above our heads as the occupying power.

They had recognised Rokuhara as Yamato's rulers and were silently watching the country fall apart. Search down to the bottom of the Ogasawara Trench: a reason to like them would probably still not be found.

And this woman looked nothing but Yamato. Naturally, words such as traitor and collaborator would present themselves.

ja.html:
彼女の方が軍服に合っているのだ。
　不穏と不吉の気配を自前で持っているのだ。
　外観がどう見えようと、彼女は間違いなく軍人なの
だから。

　あの場には村長もいた。銃声の響いた一幕を覚えて
いるのなら、今更貴婦人の仮装と誤解して戸惑うこと
もないだろう。であれば彼の困惑は実のところ、軍服
が示す所属に帰せられるに違いない。

　国際統和共栄連盟／大和進駐軍司令部。通称ＧＨＱ。
　六年前までは国を挙げての戦争相手であり、現在は
占領者として頭上に君臨する、異邦人の群団。

　そして、六波羅を大和の統治者として認め、国家の
荒廃を黙視している存在。
　好意を抱くべき理由は小笠原海溝の底まで探しても
ありそうにない。

　かてて加えて、この女性は大和人以外のどんな人種
にも見えなかった。
　自然の帰結として、売国者、裏切者、といった言語
が思い浮かぶのは避けられないところである。

Normally, the remaining business would be hostile glances, swallowed resentment and abuse after she left. All conditions satisfied. Only one small defect in the arrangement: this objectionable woman had just saved the village.

Gaali dein ya shukriya? Abuse her or thank her? The headman had finished his account and apparently run out of a safe direction for his mouth.

Should I take over? Very good. With what? My own mouth was receiving no useful instructions either.

The old woman nodded slightly. What had seemed sudden to us onlookers—myself included—had apparently arrived with an investigation already behind it. Natural enough.

Still. One long gun against a Rokuhara officer and his men. Most such officers were warriors. Prior investigation did not make the undertaking less mad. Achha, facts established, now let us get ourselves killed with complete understanding.

This person remained difficult to grasp.

Eyes narrow as pine needles turned toward me. Expression se kuch nahin mila. No readable emotion at all.
